Detail

Cleveland Guardians @ Boston Red Sox, 3:45p

Summary

This one's worth clearing your schedule for: a division-race pitching duel between two nasty lefties, with Cleveland trying to hold onto first place in the AL Central over its final six games. At 16.16, the gNERD score sits near the top of today's slate and well above the historic average, and it's easy to see why. Payton Tolle, Boston's 23-year-old rookie, brings a 10.48 pNERD — his fastball is up near 96 mph, his strikeout stuff is real, and he's fresh off the first immaculate inning by a Red Sox pitcher since Chris Sale's third career immaculate inning in 2021, plus a 14-strikeout gem against Oakland last month. Parker Messick isn't far behind at 8.38, an All-Star this year who allowed three runs over six innings with eight strikeouts in his last outing to push Cleveland into first. Both teams grade out roughly average on tNERD, with Boston getting a lift from a strong bullpen and a bit of positive batting luck suggesting they've underperformed their offensive output. Add genuine playoff stakes — Cleveland's opener of its final six regular-season games, with first place in the AL Central on the line — and you've got a legitimately compelling watch, stuff over standings.

Milwaukee Brewers @ Philadelphia Phillies, 3:40p

Summary

A late-September tilt with real stakes for one side and pure playoff-prep for the other, featuring one of baseball's best arms on the mound. The Brewers have already clinched the NL Central for a fourth straight year and are steamrolling toward the league's best record, while the Phillies are still scrapping just to hold onto a wild-card spot. Milwaukee's tNERD (9.89) reflects a genuinely fun team: strong baserunning, a shutdown bullpen, and a young, cheap roster that outperforms its payroll. Philadelphia's offense has cooled to middling territory, dragging its tNERD down to 4.68 despite a deep bullpen. The pitching matchup is the real draw — Dustin May is pitching on short rest after struggling on Friday against the Orioles, and his rest-limited outing (bettors are backing the under on his outs) contrasts sharply with Zack Wheeler, whose 8.37 pNERD is built on an elite xFIP- of 74 and one of the best swinging-strike rates in the game. With a gNERD of 14.63, comfortably above today's average of 10.77 and firmly in the upper reaches of the historical distribution, this one's worth carving out time for, mostly to watch Wheeler work.

St. Louis Cardinals @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

Jared Jones's return-from-elbow-surgery arc has quietly become one of the better pitching stories in baseball, and today he brings the best pitcher NERD score of the day into a matchup with a Pirates team playing solid all-around ball. Jones, who missed all of 2025 after internal brace surgery, came back at the end of May and has been excellent: he has pitched 90 2/3 innings in his return, with a 4.17 ERA but an improved 3.50 FIP and a 28.2% strikeout rate. His whiff rate now sits in the 94th percentile at 32.5%, and he's even flirted with history — he's thrown 6 no-hit innings this year. His pNERD of 10.51 is elite, driven by a mid-90s xFIP-, a 98-plus mph fastball, and youth on his side. Pallante, by contrast, is a solid-if-unspectacular ground-ball innings-eater for St. Louis, with his pNERD of 4.43 held down by shaky whiff and strike rates despite good velocity. On the team side, Pittsburgh's baserunning, bullpen, and even some positive batting luck push their tNERD to 7.59, well above the Cardinals' 5.80, giving this game a gNERD of 14.17 — comfortably above both the historical and today's averages, making it one of the more watchable matchups on the slate.

Miami Marlins @ Chicago Cubs, 4:40p

Summary

A high-scoring pitching mismatch wrapped in playoff stakes — the Cubs are chasing a Wild Card spot and Shota Imanaga is rounding into form at just the right time. This gNERD of 14.06 sits comfortably above the historic median (10.80) and today's average (10.77), driven largely by a strong Cubs tNERD of 10.52, fueled by Ian Happ sitting one homer shy of a top-10 all-time mark and Pete Crow-Armstrong two stolen bases from 40/40 while tied for the league lead with 45 homers. On the mound, Imanaga (pNERD 6.35, well above the 4.24 pitcher average today) is riding a stretch of three solid starts that began against these same Marlins, when he allowed just one earned run on three hits and no walks over six innings — a repeat rematch of that September 4 meeting, which the Cubs won 4-1. Janson Junk (pNERD 2.14) offers little swing-and-miss to counter him. Miami's tNERD (9.11) is buoyed almost entirely by baserunning and low payroll/age quirks rather than actual thump, and the Marlins are miserable on the road. Watch for the Cubs offense, not competitive tension.

San Diego Padres @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 7:10p

Summary

San Diego brings a five-game winning streak and a freshly punched playoff ticket into Dodger Stadium, while the Dodgers counter with... well, nobody in particular, since Los Angeles is running a bullpen game with an unclear starter — quite possibly featuring Roki Sasaki in high-leverage relief rather than a traditional turn through the rotation. That mystery-arm approach makes the pitching matchup impossible to grade, dragging the average pitcher NERD down to a modest 4.31 despite Michael King doing steady, unspectacular work for the Padres (12-9, 3.19 ERA, a tidy 1.16 WHIP) as his 3.63 pNERD suggests. The real juice here is on the team side: San Diego's 10.77 tNERD is buoyed by a shutdown bullpen and strong defense, while the Dodgers, even missing Shohei Ohtani (biceps, 15-day IL) and playing Kyle Tucker on a bad knee, still boast a lineup so potent it posts a 1.93 batting-runs z-score. Combined, a 14.03 gNERD lands comfortably above both the historical and today's averages — worth catching, mystery pitcher and all, especially with playoff seeding still very much alive for both sides.

Tampa Bay Rays @ New York Yankees, 4:05p

Summary

Rasmussen brings a legit AL Cy Young case, the Rays have already clinched the AL East, and the Yankees are missing Aaron Judge — so this is worth watching mostly because of the pitching, not the pennant race.

The Rays have wrapped up the division and enter this one having already leading New York by six games with a magic number of two, so the drama here is more about playoff seeding and personal pride than survival — both clubs have clinched postseason spots. Still, Rasmussen's pNERD of 8.20 is well above today's 5.11 average, and for good reason: he's quietly had one of the best seasons of any starter in baseball, sitting at 15-5 with a 2.72 ERA and a 0.93 WHIP, striking out 163 against just 29 walks, and he's been especially sharp lately. Fried's pNERD (4.57) is more middling, dragged down by a slow pace that costs him in the model, though his command remains strong. The Yankees' tNERD (7.35) outpaces Tampa's (4.83), fueled by a much better barrel rate, but New York is playing without Aaron Judge, who went on the 10-day injured list with a right calf strain, which takes some shine off their lineup. Add in a real division rivalry and a pitching matchup that's tighter than the moneyline suggests, and the gNERD of 12.48 — comfortably above the historical average of 10.81 — feels earned.

Minnesota Twins @ San Francisco Giants, 6:45p

Summary

Both teams are playing out the string, but the pitching matchup gives this one more juice than the standings suggest. Minnesota (73-84) and San Francisco (65-92) are long eliminated, but Taj Bradley leads the pitching staff with 199 strikeouts and 11 wins, while Luis Arraez continues hitting .324 in a lineup battered by injuries. The real draw is on the mound: Anthony Molina, just 24, posts a 9.21 pNERD—well above today's 5.11 average and near the historic 95th percentile—thanks to plus velocity, a low xFIP-, and an economical 17.3-second pace. Bradley isn't far behind at 7.40, backed by 97-mph heat and his own strong xFIP-. Both offenses are middling and both bullpens and defenses actually drag down their tNERD marks into below-average territory (3.09 and 3.36), so don't expect a crisp, clean game—Minnesota's shaky fielding and bullpen, paired with a similarly leaky Giants defense, could turn this into a track meet despite the modest run totals. At 11.53, the overall gNERD sits just above the historic median, worth a look mainly for the two arms rather than the standings race neither club is part of.

New York Mets @ Texas Rangers, 5:05p

Summary

Meaningless-standings baseball with a playoff-race twist: the Mets are dead in the water at 71-85 while the Rangers cling to a one-game lead in the AL West at 78-78, so this is Texas's game to lose down the stretch. Gore takes the ball on short professional pride after leaving his last start early with shoulder and back spasms, though he reported after the game that he felt it wasn't something that would be an issue going forward. His surface numbers look rough, but his 3.89 FIP paints a friendlier picture, and the pNERD math likes his velocity and youth. Manaea, on the other side, gets a modest bump for his elite strike-throwing and unhurried pace, plus some positive regression looming after a bit of tough luck. Neither team's offense stands out — Texas gets credit mostly for a lucky over-performance boost, and the Mets' bullpen and barrel rate keep them respectable. At 11.32, the gNERD sits a shade above today's average of 10.77, buoyed more by decent-not-great pitching than by anything the lineups are doing. Watch if you like playoff stakes on one side and irrelevant-but-competent arms on both.

On the other side, Drew Anderson, who spent years pitching in Japan and Korea before landing in Detroit, has quietly been Detroit's most reliable arm lately; over three September starts, he's allowed just four earned runs across 16 innings, and in his most recent outing he delivered five scoreless frames against Toronto. His 6.05 pNERD is comfortably above average. Washington's tNERD (8.12) is buoyed by excellent baserunning and a young, cheap roster, but a dreadful bullpen drags things down—context that matters after Detroit clubbed three homers in Monday's opener. Detroit's tNERD (3.65) is unremarkable. Overall gNERD of 10.32 sits almost exactly at today's average—watchable, not essential.

entry.title: MLB: What to watch on September 21, 2026
entry.content:
Here are today's MLB games, ordered by watchability, based on how interesting the teams and starting pitchers look. Higher is better. For more information, read this post.

Score Time (PT) Visitors Score Home Score Starter (V) Score Starter (H) Score
10.9 3:40p Washington Nationals 8.4 Detroit Tigers 3.5 DJ Herz No data River Ryan No data
8.9 3:35p Toronto Blue Jays 3.5 Baltimore Orioles 5.5 Trey Yesavage 4.9 Shane Baz 3.7
7.8 6:45p Minnesota Twins 3.1 San Francisco Giants 3.4 Zebby Matthews 6.2 Blade Tidwell 2.8

Notes:

  • Pitcher 'no data': Pitchers only have a pNERD score once they've started at least one game and have at least 20 innings pitched. I also show 'no data' when I can't correctly link a starting pitcher with their stats.
  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Washington Nationals @ Detroit Tigers, 3:40p

Summary

Two pitchers, two Tommy John surgeries, two comeback stories — this game is basically a science experiment in rust, and that's exactly why it's worth a look. DJ Herz makes his first big-league start since September 2024, having missed two years recovering from Tommy John surgery, with a June setback further slowing things down. Opposite him, River Ryan makes his Detroit debut after being traded from the Dodgers to the Tigers, along with two other players, in exchange for Tarik Skubal, and hasn't pitched in the majors since 2024 himself. Neither arm has meaningful workload data this year — Herz reached only 65 pitches in his last Triple-A outing, putting roughly four innings as a realistic ceiling — so both pNERD scores sit at zero simply because there's nothing to measure yet, not because they're bad. The real juice here is on the offensive side: Washington's tNERD of 8.37 is buoyed by strong baserunning and barrel rates, though a shaky bullpen drags it back down. Detroit's tNERD is more middling. With two teams that have already checked out of the playoff race, today's 10.91 gNERD ranks solidly above the day's 9.18 average — worth watching mostly for the novelty, not the stakes.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Baltimore Orioles, 4:20p

Summary

Here's the summary:

This one's near the top of the day's slate for a reason: Jacob Misiorowski is must-watch theater, and Baltimore's depleted lineup gives him plenty of room to work. Misiorowski, this year's presumptive NL Cy Young frontrunner, has a 1.89 ERA with a 2.08 xERA and a 2.19 FIP over 166.1 innings, averaging 100.5 mph with his fastball and striking out 243 batters. What makes the 24-year-old's season remarkable isn't just velocity — he's issued just 42 walks for a 6.6% BB%, a stunning turnaround for a guy who once walked hitters at a double-digit clip in the minors. His 15.00 pNERD is essentially max-scale, built on elite strikeout stuff, a hellacious xFIP-, and youth. Brandon Young, by contrast, offers a modest 3.40 pNERD and a fringe-average four-seamer. The Orioles are limping toward the finish line — fighting for playoff survival at 75-80 with a -28 run differential, without Jackson Holliday, Luis Robert Jr., Tyler O'Neill, and Ryan Mountcastle all injured simultaneously. Milwaukee's tNERD (9.85) reflects a genuinely fun, young, athletic roster with plus baserunning and bullpen depth. This gNERD of 16.96 sits well above today's average and near the top of the historical distribution — tune in for the Miz, stay for the mismatch.

Playoff-race backdrop meets a season-finale-ish rubber match that's got more juice than the standings might suggest. The Padres (85-69) are locked in behind a deep, well-drummed bullpen and a fielding unit that's quietly been excellent, while the Marlins, playing out the string at 76-78, still bring real teeth against right-handed pitching this month. The Marlins quietly slot inside the Top-10 in average, wOBA, and SLG against righties this month, which matters because Fernando Tatis Jr. is crushing Alcantara's pitch mix, managing an impressive .333 ISO with a 20.7% barrel rate in their recent history — a genuine swing-through storyline worth tracking. Alcantara still pumps mid-to-upper-90s heat and posts the better pNERD of the two arms, though Buehler owns a middling 4.16 xFIP over the past 30 days, so neither is exactly locked in. San Diego's tNERD (10.93) ranks near the top of today's slate, boosted by a strong bullpen and top-tier broadcast crew, and the Padres bring real quality to Petco. The overall gNERD of 14.91 sits comfortably above both the historical and today's averages — a solidly watchable one, buoyed more by team quality and a live individual matchup than by big pitching numbers.

That alone makes this more watchable than the raw numbers suggest, and the numbers aren't bad either — a 12.10 gNERD sits solidly above the historical median and roughly in line with today's slate average.

The Cincinnati Reds and the Chicago Cubs have split the first two games of the series, and Chicago could clinch a playoff spot with a win combined with a loss by Arizona. The Twins own baseball's worst last-place club by the numbers, and this Angels team isn't much better off—both squads carry ugly fielding and baserunning marks, with Los Angeles's offense also cratering to the bottom of the league. The Angels won the opener, lost the next game 3-0, then beat the Twins 6-5 in 11 innings, part of a stretch that has them at 60-95, in last place in the AL West. On the mound, Johnson enters at 5-8 with a 4.88 ERA, but has worked exactly six innings in each of his last three starts, and yes, he's still doing that unique warm-up routine that includes handstands in the bullpen. Kremer, mixing up his pitches in a new home after leaving Baltimore, carries a modest pNERD boost mostly from pure luck—his xFIP suggests he's been fortunate, not dominant. Both team NERDs sit near the bottom of today's slate, and the gNERD of 5.66 lands well below the historical average, so this one's mostly for Twins or Angels die-hards.

Miami Marlins @ San Diego Padres, 5:40p

Summary

San Diego's playoff push meets Miami's lame-duck reality, and the Padres bring by far the juicier storyline here. With a gNERD of 15.56 — comfortably above the historical 95th percentile and near the top of today's slate — this one's worth your remote.

San Diego enters riding a hot stretch that has them pushed to 85-69 on the season and pulled into a three-way tie for the wild card spots in the National League, while Miami has already been eliminated from the postseason race, so only one dugout has anything at stake. Making matters worse for the Marlins, their bullpen is a genuine wreck — Andrew Nardi, Anthony Bender, Pete Fairbanks, and William Kempner are all unavailable. On the mound, Eury Pérez is the real draw: 23 years old, sitting 98 mph, and posting the best pNERD of the night (7.14) thanks to elite velocity and whiff rates. Casey Mize is comparatively unspectacular (pNERD 4.19), a fine innings-eater rather than a show-stealer. San Diego's tNERD (10.72) leans heavily on a dominant bullpen and top-shelf fielding — the engine behind their surge — making this a legitimately watchable pairing of contender urgency and individual pitching intrigue.

San Francisco Giants @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 6:10p

Summary

Tarik Skubal doing Tarik Skubal things is reason enough to tune in, even if the Giants' half of this game is a mystery. The Dodgers grabbed Skubal at the deadline in a blockbuster that cost them serious prospect capital, and he's rewarded them with exactly the swing-and-miss dominance you'd expect from a two-time Cy Young winner — his 11.96 pNERD sits near the top of the scale we track, and this outing marks his final regular season start at Dodger Stadium this season, pitching on four days' rest for just the second time this month. San Francisco's counterpart is a total TBD, contributing nothing to the pitching math and adding a bit of intrigue by omission. The Dodgers' lineup (8.52 tNERD) dwarfs the Giants' punchless 3.52, backed by real batting and bullpen strength, while San Francisco limps in as a team whose 64-89 record makes late-September relevance mostly theoretical. At 14.50, the gNERD clears both the historical 95th percentile (15.60) and today's average handily — mostly on Skubal's arm alone, so watch for the strikeouts and stick around only if the Giants can make it interesting.

New York Yankees @ Arizona Diamondbacks, 5:10p

Summary

A potential Cy Young front-runner takes the mound in the desert, and even without Aaron Judge in the lineup, this one's worth your attention. Cam Schlittler comes in carrying a 1.95 ERA and 228 strikeouts, and just passed Whitey Ford, Ron Guidry, and Jack Chesbro for the most starts with 1 run or less allowed in Yankees history — his pNERD of 10.96, built on elite xFIP-, 98-mph heat, and a hefty swinging-strike rate, is comfortably above today's average and near the historic 95th percentile. The bad news for New York: the Yankees are expected to place Judge on the 10-day injured list Saturday due to a right calf strain, though the lineup still has Bellinger, Rice and Volpe to lean on. Brandon Pfaadt is the far less flashy pitching story, a league-average arm (pNERD 4.11) with a 3.77 ERA and 84 strikeouts giving Arizona a chance to hang around. Team-wise the Yankees' tNERD (7.46) outpaces Arizona's (5.58), fueled by New York's barrel rate, while Arizona's speed and defense keep it from being a mismatch — Corbin Carroll and Geraldo Perdomo's stolen-base game remains a weapon even when the offense stalls. The 14.06 gNERD lands well above both the historic and today's averages, making this a solid watch.

Milwaukee's lineup and bullpen numbers are legitimately strong across the board, giving them the best team score of anyone on the slate today, while the Orioles, playing out a lost season, still bring enough contact-quality and pop off the bat to keep things from getting boring.

On the mound, Robert Gasser (4-5, 4.30 ERA, 4.32 FIP) is still auditioning for a spot in Milwaukee's rotation come postseason time, and he'll be making his first career appearance against Baltimore. A middling gNERD score dressed up by two live young arms worth watching, even if the standings say otherwise. Kansas City's playoff hopes are long dead (67-87, buried in the AL Central) and Pittsburgh is treading water at .500, but this one's really about the pitchers. Noah Cameron has been quietly one of the better second-half starters in the league, the season line undersells him — since the All-Star break he has posted a 2.42 ERA and a 0.88 WHIP over roughly 70 innings, and his NERD components reward his low walk rate and youth even if his velocity is unremarkable. Across the mound, 23-year-old Bubba Chandler brings a wholly different profile: he's still just a rookie building his track record after debuting on August 22, 2025, becoming the first Pirates pitcher to record a save in his MLB debut, and his NERD score leans almost entirely on triple-digit heat rather than command, with a walk rate to match. Pittsburgh's tNERD edges Kansas City's thanks to a bullpen that's actually performing while the Royals' pen has been dreadful, though a positive Royals luck score suggests Kansas City's offense has underperformed and could be an out-away from breaking out. Not essential, but not empty calories either.

The Mets, despite a five-game losing streak, still get a mild tNERD edge (5.37 vs 4.72) thanks to better barrel rates and a notably strong broadcast crew rating on both TV and radio. Neither team's bats are impressing anyone — both Philly and New York post negative batting-runs marks — but both bullpens are quietly solid, which should keep things competitive into the late innings.

Pitching-wise, we're flying blind: Philadelphia's starter is still TBD, and Mets righty Zac Thornton has no NERD data on file, though he's carrying a 3.44 ERA into the start. With both pNERD scores sitting at zero, this game's 10.04 gNERD lands almost exactly at today's slate average of 11.60 — not a must-watch, but the standings drama and a five-game Mets skid give it a pulse. The Phillies lead the season series, having won five of the nine meetings between these clubs, so there's a little history for the taking.

Milwaukee Brewers @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 9:35a

Summary

A late-season laugher on paper, but the NERD math says pay attention anyway. Milwaukee's Brewers, fresh off clinching the NL Central at a franchise-record 36 games over .500, are chasing a sweep in Pittsburgh, while a Pirates team playing out the string has quietly set a single-season home run record. The 18.44 gNERD sits near the top of today's slate (7.94–18.44) and comfortably above the historic 95th percentile of 15.6, driven by two lively lineups—Milwaukee's power-and-speed combo (tNERD 9.93) and Pittsburgh's surprisingly frisky bats (tNERD 7.08) despite shaky fielding. Harrison has struggled lately, giving up 19 runs across his last three outings, but he's dominated Pittsburgh specifically, going 2-0 in three career starts without allowing a run in 17 innings. His pNERD (10.55) reflects real swing-and-miss stuff and a positive luck score suggesting better days ahead. Dotel, just 23 and making only his second career start, brings a 1.36 WHIP in a limited big-league sample but nasty velocity that props up his 9.34 pNERD—worth watching for the arm talent alone.

Nolan McLean, still just 24 and a season removed from his MLB debut, has quietly built a 3.24 ERA over 166.2 innings and comes with the best pNERD in this matchup (7.53) thanks to plus xFIP-, a lively 95.5 mph fastball, and a young-and-quick-working profile that keeps things moving. Aaron Nola brings the name recognition but a rougher season line — he's actually pitched much better of late, posting a 3.60 ERA over his last nine starts while allowing 3+ runs just once — and his solid pNERD (5.33) is boosted by positive luck, suggesting his ugly full-season homer total undersells his recent form. Watch for Juan Soto, who has historically teed off on Nola over the years, posting a .283 average, .391 ISO, and left the park five times over 46 at-bats. New York's bullpen is thin — Devin Williams and Cionel Perez are both on the 15-day IL, along with Robert Stock and Daniel Duarte, meaning four relievers are out, which could turn a tight game messy late. The Mets' 5.52 tNERD narrowly edges Philadelphia's 4.70, and the overall 11.54 gNERD sits a bit above today's average (10.84), making this a reasonably solid pick without being a must-watch.

Overall gNERD of 10.54 lands right around league average, a fine but unspectacular way to spend three hours.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

The best pitching matchup of the day, wrapped in a division-clinching afterglow — this one's worth your evening. Fresh off popping champagne for their fourth straight NL Central title, the Brewers roll into PNC Park with baseball's top gNERD score today (17.74), and the arms are the reason why. Rookie Logan Henderson (10-3, 2.34 ERA) starts as he tries to push the Brewers toward the NL's top seed, opposing Jared Jones in a rematch of their August 4 meeting in Milwaukee, which the Brewers won 4-2. Henderson's a legitimately fun watch: he has issued only 15 free passes all season, and he has never allowed more than three runs in any of his 20 career starts. Jones, whose 9.87 pNERD tops the day thanks to elite velocity and whiff rates, has been quietly dazzling himself — he hasn't allowed a run in his past two starts, a stretch of 13 innings. Milwaukee's lineup backs it up, ranking near the top of the league in batting and baserunning value, with a young, cost-efficient roster that overperforms its payroll. Pittsburgh's offense is thin, but strong bullpen and baserunning marks keep them respectable. Two power arms, a playoff-seeding subplot, and a division champ still hungry — good stuff.

A basement-dweller against a division leader coasting toward October rarely screams "must-watch," but there's just enough juice here to make it a decent afternoon watch. Tampa Bay (91-59, AL East leaders) is riding a four-game home winning streak against an Athletics team that's 61-90 overall and 32-44 on the road, and this is the fifth meeting between these two this season, with the Rays up 4-0. Nick Martinez has quietly had an All-Star-caliber year — 14-4 with a 2.92 ERA and 1.07 WHIP over 166 1/3 innings — but his xFIP- of 108 suggests some regression is fair, and his 3.34 pNERD reflects a modest package built mostly on strike-throwing rather than bat-missing. Brady Basso, filling a rotation hole created by injuries to J.T. Ginn (elbow, 15-day IL) and Gage Jump (shoulder), is the more interesting arm statistically, with a tidier xFIP- (93) pushing his pNERD to 5.72 despite modest strikeout stuff. Tampa Bay's offense is playing far better than expected (positive batting-runs, +0.98 z-score) while the barrel rate is oddly low for a good-hitting team — a quirky contrast worth noting. With a gNERD of 8.30, this sits below the historical average (10.81) and near the low end of today's slate (6.09–17.74), so treat it as background baseball rather than appointment viewing.

I've got enough to write the summary now.

Two teams playing out very different stakes but neither pitcher inspires much confidence, so this one's for completists and Astros-race watchers more than anyone chasing must-see baseball. The pitching matchup is a legitimate step down in quality: Cristian Javier owns a 5.50 ERA and 8.9 strikeouts per nine innings this season, and while his one earned run over six innings against Philadelphia last time out was encouraging, his underlying command issues (a pace that's glacial by NERD standards) keep his pNERD modest. Daniel Lynch has been shaky too — he's 1-3 with a 6.31 ERA over seven starts since joining the rotation on Aug. 7 — though he does own a fun quirk of dominance against this exact opponent, going 2-0 with a 1.26 ERA across five career appearances against the Astros, including consecutive perfect relief outings in mid-June. With a gNERD of just 6.09 — below both the historic and today's-slate averages — and two below-average offenses (Toronto's barrel rate is particularly ugly), this one's mostly for Tigers fans enjoying the ride.

entry.content:
Here are today's MLB games, ordered by watchability, based on how interesting the teams and starting pitchers look. Higher is better. For more information, read this post.

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

Milwaukee's magic number to clinch the NL Central is two, and Jacob Misiorowski's turn to pitch happens to fall right at the moment they could clinch it. This is appointment viewing: the game's top pitcher NERD score of the day belongs to a Cy Young frontrunner who could clinch a division title while touching 100+ mph, against a Pittsburgh bullpen game that exists mostly to survive nine innings.

Misiorowski has been, in the words of one outlet, "the favorite to win the NL Cy Young Award this year", sporting a 1.95 ERA and a 2.24 FIP with 236 strikeouts, and opponents are hitting just .156 against him this season. His pNERD of 14.73 is comfortably above today's field (max 14.73, average 5.46) thanks to elite strikeout stuff (100.6 mph average velocity) and a tiny xFIP-. Across from him, Lake Bachar is functionally a bullpen-game placeholder — Pittsburgh has used a bullpen game in that rotation spot led off by reliever Lake Bachar (1-3, 3.52) the last three turns through the starting order — and his 3.84 pNERD reflects the mismatch. The Brewers' 9.93 tNERD (elite baserunning, bullpen, and a young, cheap roster) dwarfs Pittsburgh's 6.83, though the Pirates aren't dead yet in the wild-card race and still bring solid baserunning and bullpen marks of their own. With a 17.67 gNERD, this sits near the top of both today's slate and the historical distribution — worth clearing your schedule for, division-clinch drama included.

Philadelphia Phillies @ Washington Nationals, 3:45p

Summary

Sánchez leads MLB in wins and is coming off a rough outing against Houston, worth watching to see if he bounces back against a Nationals lineup that's playing spoiler with nothing but pride at stake.

The Phillies are still clinging to faint NL East hopes while the Nationals are already eliminated from contention, but Washington's youth and aggression on the bases make them a surprisingly lively watch late in a lost season. Sánchez brings by far the better arm here — his xFIP- of 62 is elite, and his season line reflects it: he leads MLB in wins this season, off his worst outing since July after giving up six earned runs to the Astros. He'll need to be sharper against Washington, a team he's already beaten once this year in an August start. On the other side, rookie lefty Jackson Kent is still finding his footing — he carries a 6.59 ERA and a 1.83 WHIP through six big-league starts, with 23 strikeouts and 20 walks across 27.1 innings, and his strike-throwing woes show up clearly in his below-average pNERD components. The Nationals' tNERD actually outpaces Philadelphia's, powered by strong baserunning and barrel rates, but a shaky bullpen keeps this from being a truly high-end matchup. A solidly average gNERD day, elevated mostly by Sánchez.

Boston Red Sox @ Texas Rangers, 5:05p

Summary

A late-season, low-stakes-for-one-team affair salvaged almost entirely by watching a 38-year-old legend still humming mid-90s heat. Jacob deGrom, five years removed from his last true ace peak, is putting together a genuine comeback season in Arlington — he's Texas's strikeout leader and still pumping 97.4 mph, backing an xFIP- of 72 that ranks among the best NERD scores you'll see all year (pNERD 11.40, well above today's 14.73 ceiling but still elite). The Rangers, sitting a game back of a playoff spot, need him locked in, and their bullpen and lineup (Josh Jung and Wyatt Langford heating up) give this game a bit of juice. Seattle leads the division by a comfortable margin, but a three-game losing streak is the kind of thing that can tighten a race quickly, while the Angels, 18 games back, are not a playoff factor but have been a credible opponent at home.   • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Chicago White Sox @ Cleveland Guardians, 3:40p

Summary

A legitimate ace on the mound and a playoff race hanging in the balance make this the best watch of the day. Gavin Williams has quietly turned into a Cy Young dark horse this year, not named an All-Star but the type of pitcher who "wouldn't be surprising whatsoever" to get Cy Young votes come November, and he passed 200 strikeouts on August 20th. His 12.71 pNERD is elite - a 67 xFIP-, mid-90s velocity, and a filthy strikeout rate all point to a pitcher who can miss bats and rack up value in a hurry. Newcomb is a serviceable complement with an 89-good xFIP- but nothing special, and his fringe stuff and lack of consistency mean this game leans heavily on Williams' shoulders. The stakes matter too: the AL Central rivals are jockeying for postseason positioning, with Cleveland fighting to hang onto its wild-card grip while Chicago sits atop the division. Both offenses carry youth and low payrolls that boost their tNERD marks, though Cleveland's below-average barrel rate is a real soft spot. At 16.73, this gNERD sits well above today's 11.03 average and near the historical 95th percentile - genuinely one of the better games on the board.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Cincinnati Reds, 3:40p

Summary

Skubal on the mound is reason enough to tune in—the reigning two-time AL Cy Young winner has been a revelation since arriving from Detroit, and this is a rematch of the beatdown he put on Cincinnati just last week. In that September 9 start, he worked into the eighth inning against these same Reds, allowing just two runs on four hits with five strikeouts across 7 1/3 innings. His pNERD of 11.91 is comfortably above today's slate average, driven by elite whiff and strike rates and a fastball that still sits at 96.8 mph. Across his run with LA, Skubal is 2-2 with a 2.93 ERA and 48 strikeouts over 43 innings, and his xFIP- suggests he's actually pitching even better than that shiny ERA implies.

Lodolo, by contrast, is the exact opposite story — a 2.03 pNERD reflecting a rough season where his last three starts have been even shakier at a 5.52 ERA, with command issues (38 walks) fueling the mismatch. The Reds counter with some thump — De La Cruz has been an absolute terror at the plate, crushing a 444-foot home run off Skubal on September 9 — but the Dodgers own a clear tNERD edge (8.02 to 4.75), buoyed by strong batting and bullpen numbers. At 13.35, this game's gNERD lands solidly above the historical median and near today's average, making it a reasonably watchable pick, mostly on the strength of watching an ace work.

Miami Marlins @ Arizona Diamondbacks, 6:40p

Summary

Not exactly a marquee pitching duel on paper, but the backstory carries this one: Corbin Burnes making just his second start back from Tommy John surgery, still on a strict pitch count, against a Marlins team clinging to fading wild-card hopes. Sandy Alcantara has been the workhorse of the National League — he leads the majors with 21 quality starts and 200 innings pitched, the first time he's hit that plateau since his 2022 Cy Young season — but he's been scuffling lately, allowing 11 earned runs over just 10.1 innings across his last two September starts. Burnes, meanwhile, looked sharp in his return, tossing three scoreless innings on 57 pitches against Kansas City, though his cutter velocity is still a tick down from last year. Since Burnes has no track record yet this season, his pNERD sits at zero, dragging the pitching score down despite Alcantara's plus fastball velocity carrying his end. The Marlins' tNERD (8.97) stands out thanks to strong baserunning, a young inexpensive roster, and some positive regression-to-come luck, while Arizona's solid defense keeps its offer respectable. Overall gNERD of 12.38 sits comfortably above the historical and today's averages — watchable, if only to see how far Burnes can stretch it.

On the mound, Will Warren (4.90 pNERD) has quietly solid peripherals backing his 10-6 mark, and while Dean Kremer's surface numbers are rougher, his xFIP- suggests he's been unlucky and due for better results than his rocky ERA implies. Neither arm brings big strikeout stuff, so don't expect a strikeout clinic. At a 10.21 gNERD, this sits almost exactly at the historical median and slightly below today's average slate, so it's a perfectly reasonable game if the Yankees' pursuit of the AL East title interests you, but there are better-watch options on the board today.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Miami Marlins, 10:40a

Summary

A high-strikeout, high-drama series finale that ranks near the top of the day's watchability board, thanks to two hard-throwing arms who can't quite stay out of their own way. This one caps a weekend set in Miami with the Dodgers (90-58, riding an 8-2 stretch) looking to close out the Marlins (73-76, losers of seven of ten) in a dome that's been pitcher-friendly all year. Emmet Sheehan's 5.08 ERA undersells him — he's racked up 118 strikeouts in 101 innings and just struck out 10 over 5.2 innings in a 6-3 win over Cincinnati, and his pNERD (7.29) reflects a nasty swinging-strike rate and youthful upside. Eury Pérez, at just 23 with a mid-90s-plus fastball touching 98, has been electric but leaky lately — he's allowed five-plus runs while failing to reach the fifth inning in three straight outings, walking four against Washington and three against the Mets. Both bullpens are taxed after a bullpen-heavy Saturday, adding some late-inning intrigue. With a gNERD of 15.66 — comfortably above today's 11.35 average and near the historic 95th percentile — and Miami's tNERD boosted by youth, baserunning, and some positive luck, this game earns its spot near the top of the watch list even without a marquee team on paper.

Summary

A Subway Series finale with legitimate Cy Young intrigue on the mound and a rivalry that's already delivered fireworks this weekend. Cam Schlittler brings an AL-best mark and a strikeout total befitting a genuine Cy Young frontrunner, and the underlying numbers back it up — his xFIP- sits nearly two standard deviations better than league average, with mid-90s-plus velocity and a swinging-strike rate that leads to a pNERD score comfortably above today's average and well into historically elite territory. Christian Scott is the clear undercard, a serviceable arm with a solid strikeout rate but nothing that jumps off the page. The Yankees' offense, powered by Ben Rice's big year, gives them the higher tNERD of the two clubs, while the Mets counter with the better broadcast booth and a barrel rate that keeps their lineup dangerous despite a middling season. This is also revenge-game territory: New York's NL side torched Gerrit Cole for a 12-2 rout the day before, so the Yankees will want their ace-in-waiting to settle things down. With the Yankees fighting for AL East ground and the wild card, and a gNERD score near the top of today's slate, this one's worth carving out time for.
